chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who becomes junub: is it sufficient for his ghusl al-janabah that he stand in the rain until he washes his head and body, while he is able to do otherwise? He said: “If it washes him as his washing with water would, that suffices him.”
Then he said—may Allah, Most High, support him: it is not appropriate for him to immerse himself in still water, for if it is a small amount, he corrupts it.

The correct understanding in this is that the junub has the ruling of the najis until he performs ghusl, so whenever he comes into contact with water that can validly receive impurity, it becomes spoiled. This does not contradict the following hadith which...
(425) 116. It was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ibn Miskān, who said: Muḥammad ibn Muyassir narrated to me; he said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a junub man who comes upon a small amount of water on the road and wants to perform ghusl from it, but he has no vessel with which to scoop from it, and his hands are dirty. He said: “He places his hand in it, performs wudu (ablution), and performs ghusl. This is from what Allah, Most High, has said:”
“He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship.”

Because the meaning of this report is that he should take the water from the pool with his hand and not enter it himself, and perform ghusl by pouring it over the body. But if he enters it, it becomes spoiled, according to what we have explained; this indicates what we have mentioned.

key_terms.النَّجَاسَةِ: ritual impurity that affects the legal status of water
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الرَّاكِدِ: still water that is not flowing
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْقَلِيلِ: a small quantity of water subject to impurity rulings
key_terms.الْمَطَرِ: rain used as water for purification
key_terms.حَرَجٍ: undue hardship or constriction in religious law
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required after janabah

ai.seo_question: Does standing in the rain count as ghusl al-janabah, and can a junub person use a small amount of water for purification?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses legal rulings concerning ghusl al-janabah, especially washing in rainwater and the use of a small amount of still water. It indicates that rain may suffice for ghusl if the body is washed properly, while also distinguishing between drawing water from a small pool and entering it directly, with reference to the Qur’anic principle that religion does not impose hardship.
